question: Does waking on events, instead of re-prompting every few seconds, cut model calls per hour and cost per level without slowing progress?
note: All three arms run the harness/wake build of 53214930, pinned by digest. All three arms run that one image, so harness drift cannot separate them: the control passes no wake flag and runs the branch with both options off, which renders master's prompt byte for byte and paces as master does; the arms differ only in their args, and a treatment run records its options in config.wake and in the comparability tuple, where a control run records none. The leash is e90's (90 minutes, idle and no-XP at 20 minutes, the 3000-call guard), so a cell reads against e90 history as well as against its own control; the idle watchdog sits well above the five-minute wake cap. One cell, the subscription lanes' calibration start. Assignments are the store row's, not the definition's: the first is the roster entry sub-haiku-55 (Claude Haiku 5.5 on claude-code) on all three arms, set in campaigns/wake-probe once this version is published (operator, 2026-10-19).

cells.note: The subscription lanes' scored start: the calibration cell.

arms.note: The branch image with both wake options off: a reply without a tool call is re-prompted after the 3 s step, as on master.
A reply without a tool call sleeps until a wake fires (death, stream closed, sandbox restart, harness notice, level-up, quest objectives done) or five minutes pass.
The turn-end wake, plus the ambient wait({ on, maxMs }) that holds a snippet open up to five minutes for a named event, a promise or a predicate.
